issue.description: rustup keeps its toolchains under ~/.rustup and its command shims under ~/.cargo/bin, but that directory is not part of the PATH of a fresh login shell. `cargo` and `rustc` are therefore not found.
evidence: ~/.cargo/bin is not in the login shell PATH
issue.impact: `command not found: cargo`, or a different Rust toolchain than the one rustup manages (rustup override/toolchain selection has no effect).
issue.recommended_action: Add `. "$HOME/.cargo/env"` to ~/.zshrc (this is the line the rustup installer adds), or `export PATH="~/.cargo/bin:$PATH"`.
issue.title: Rust is installed but `cargo` and `rustc` are not in PATH

issue.description: Python is installed through Homebrew, macOS / Command Line Tools, uv. Each installation has its own packages; which one runs depends on PATH order.
issue.impact: Not a problem by itself, but it is the usual root cause of `pip` installing into the wrong place and of `python` behaving differently between terminals and editors.
issue.recommended_action: Keep the installations you actively use and uninstall the rest (for Homebrew: `brew uninstall python@3.x`; for pyenv: `pyenv uninstall <version>`). Use the Command Resolution page to see which one wins.
issue.title: 3 Python installations from 3 different sources

issue.description: /etc/paths.d/10-pmk-global adds /pkg/env/global/bin to every user's PATH, but the directory does not exist. It was left behind by an installer whose package has since been removed.
issue.impact: Harmless; every command lookup checks one dead directory.
issue.recommended_action: Remove the file with administrator rights (`sudo rm /etc/paths.d/10-pmk-global`) if the tool is gone. DevDoctor never modifies system files.
issue.title: System PATH entry does not exist: /pkg/env/global/bin
